title: Function Template
description: Define a function template that works with any type
explanation: Function templates generate type-specific functions at compile time.

title: Multiple Template Parameters
description: Function template with multiple type parameters
explanation: Multiple template parameters allow different types for different arguments.

title: Non Type Template Parameter
description: Pass compile-time constant values as template parameters
explanation: Non-type template parameters accept compile-time constants like ints, enums, and pointers.

title: Template Default Type
description: Provide default type for template parameter
explanation: Default template types allow usage without specifying the type explicitly.

title: Function Template Specialization
description: Provide type-specific implementation for a function template
explanation: Template specializations override the generic implementation for specific types.

title: Class Template
description: Define a class that works with any type
explanation: Class templates define type-independent class blueprints.

title: Class Template Specialization
description: Full specialization of a class template for a specific type
explanation: Full class specialization provides a completely different implementation for a specific type.

title: Partial Template Specialization
description: Specialize only part of the template parameters
explanation: Partial specialization matches a subset of template parameter combinations.

title: Template Template Parameter
description: Pass a template as a template parameter
explanation: Template template parameters allow parameterizing a template with another template.

title: Variadic Template Function
description: Function template accepting any number of arguments (C++11)
explanation: Variadic templates accept any number of arguments using parameter packs.

title: Sizeof Variadic Pack
description: Count number of arguments in a parameter pack
explanation: sizeof... returns the number of elements in a parameter pack at compile time.

title: Variadic Class Template
description: Class template with variadic type parameters
explanation: Variadic class templates enable flexible type-safe heterogeneous containers.

title: Type Traits Is Same
description: Check if two types are the same at compile time (C++11)
explanation: is_same checks type equality at compile time, commonly used with if constexpr.

title: Type Traits Categories
description: Common type category traits for introspection (C++11)
explanation: Type category traits identify the fundamental kind of a type at compile time.

title: Type Traits Type Modifications
description: Transform types by adding or removing qualifiers (C++11)
explanation: Type modification traits add or remove cv-qualifiers, references, and pointers.

title: Enable If SFINAE
description: Conditionally enable templates using SFINAE (C++11)
explanation: enable_if removes function overloads from consideration when the condition is false, leveraging SFINAE.

title: Conditional Type Selector
description: Select type at compile time based on a boolean condition (C++11)
code:
#include <type_traits>

template<int N>
using int_type = conditional_t<
    (N <= 127), int8_t,
    conditional_t<(N <= 32767), int16_t,
    conditional_t<(N <= 2147483647), int32_t, int64_t>
    >>;

int_type<100> a;    // int8_t
int_type<40000> b;  // int16_t

// Another example:
template<typename T>
using ValueType = conditional_t<
    is_same_v<T, string>, const char*, T>;

ValueType<int> x = 42;         // int
ValueType<string> y = "test"; // const char*
explanation: conditional_t is a compile-time ternary operator for types, often used for type metaprogramming.

title: Common Type
description: Find the common type that two types can convert to (C++11)
explanation: common_type finds the type to which both types can be implicitly converted.

title: Underlying Type
description: Get the underlying integer type of an enum (C++11)
explanation: underlying_type extracts the integer type underlying an enumeration.

title: Void T Detection Idiom
description: Detect if a type has a member or nested type using void_t (C++17)
explanation: void_t simplifies SFINAE for checking type properties like member types and functions.

title: CRTP Pattern
description: Static polymorphism via the Curiously Recurring Template Pattern
explanation: CRTP enables static polymorphism (compile-time virtual dispatch) without virtual function overhead.

title: Alias Template
description: Create a template type alias using 'using' (C++11)
explanation: Alias templates simplify complex template expressions and fix template parameters.

title: Template Template Function
description: Function accepting any container template as parameter
explanation: Template template parameters in functions adapt to any standard container type.

title: Template Template Variadic
description: Combine variadic and template template parameters
explanation: Combining variadic templates with template template parameters provides maximum flexibility.

title: Static Assert With Templates
description: Compile-time assertions in template code (C++11)
explanation: static_assert fails compilation with a custom message when the condition is false.

title: Template Argument Deduction
description: Compiler deduces template arguments from function/constructor calls
explanation: Template argument deduction saves the programmer from specifying types explicitly.

title: Template Template CRTP Mixin
description: Multiple CRTP mixins to compose behavior
explanation: Multiple CRTP mixins compose independent behaviors without virtual inheritance overhead.

title: Template Specialization For Pointers
description: Partial specialization for pointer types
explanation: Partial specialization for pointers enables type-aware utility functions.

title: Integer Sequence (C++14)
description: Compile-time integer sequences for tuple/array operations (C++14)
explanation: integer_sequence enables compile-time iteration over indices for tuple-like types.

title: Mutable Template Lambda (C++23)
description: Recursive and mutable lambdas with explicit 'this' (C++23)
explanation: Deducing this (C++23) allows lambdas to reference themselves recursively without std::function.
